messages.subject: Discussion on human-exon-array-analysis
parts:
Hello,

I am following the steps to analyze the exon array data at
ftp://ftp1.nci.nih.gov/tcga/tumor/gbm/cgcc/lbl.gov/huex-1_0-st-v2/exon/lbl.gov_GBM.HuEx-1_0-st-v2.1.3.0/

But I get the following messages when I either take the first 4 or
20 .CEL files

# To examine NUSE and RLE plots, do
qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
plotNuse(qam)

#Test with 4 and 20 arrays, both get the following error messages.
#Error in plot.window(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, log = log, yaxs = pars
$yaxs) :
# need finite 'ylim' values
#In addition: Warning messages:
#1: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
#2: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

It appears that all values in qam are 0. Any comments?

Thanks.

Gang

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Discussion on human-exon-array-analysis
parts:
Hi Gang,
Can you send us all the code that led up to that (i.e. the fitting of
the plm model, what cdf you used, etc.) I assume you didn't get any
errors earlier? Can you tell us the output from sessionInfo()?

The code should work, but you can also try
ces<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
plotBoxplot(ces, type="NUSE")

In addition, to spot-check try the following and see if the answers make
sense

ces<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
cesMat<-extractMatrix(ces,units=1:10,field="theta") #get the chip effect
estimates for first 10 units
cesNuse<-extractMatrix(ces,units=1:10,field="NUSE") #get the Nuse values
cesBxp<-calculateNuseBoxplotStats(ces) #calculates the boxplot summary
statistics

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Discussion on human-exon-array-analysis
parts:
Hi Elizabeth,

The following is the code:

library(aroma.affymetrix)

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
timestampOn(verbose)

#Getting annotation data files
#chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
#cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType, tags="core")
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromFile("HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.cdf")
print(cdf)
 
# Defining CEL set
#Next we setup the CEL set with the above custom CDF:

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles(".", cdf=cdf)
print(cs)

#Background Adjustment and Normalization
#In order to do RMA background correction, we setup a correction method and runs it by:

bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose)
print(csBC)

#We then setup a quantile normalization method:
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
print(qn)

#and we then run it by:

csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
print(csN)
#This will take approx 30-60s per array. 
 
#Summarization
#To treat transcripts as units, do:
plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
print(plm)
 
# QC

# To examine NUSE and RLE plots, do
qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
plotNuse(qam)

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Discussion on human-exon-array-analysis
parts:
Hi Gang,
So you are using aroma.affymetrix_0.8.3; this is an old version. There
was a substantial update recently and the new version is 0.9.0. The code
for the NUSE/RLE boxplots was completely rewritten because there was an
error in the code--though not the same as you got, necessarily, but it's
possible that it's related. Certainly all the zeros you are getting are
because of this.

Please update (see instructions on the group pages), try again, and let
us know if that fixes the problem.

The code I sent you to test out will not work without the new version
either, which you may have discovered. You don't need to refit your
previous work since they should be fine.

Best,
Elizabeth

Hi Mark,

I was wondering how I could check up the quality of my arrays. I would
like to be able to use the normalised data produced by aroma and do a
preRMA and postRMA boxplot and histogram and then illustrate the MA
plots of my data. Would that be sufficient to make sure the data is of
good quality ?

Thanks a lot in advance,
Mathieu Parent
McGill University
